_comment: OSF registration update 3 for osf.io/ab2wn: amendment 9 and the Phase 4 outcomes. Update 2 (amendments 2-8) was approved 2026-09-23; amendment 9 came after it. File with: python scripts/osf_update.py --responses data/osf/update3_responses.json
_justification: Amendment 9 and the completion of coding. (9) ABSENCE IS NOT SILENCE. Two general rules in the coding manual contradicted each other on the commonest judgement in coding. Rule 2 told a coder who cannot point at evidence to record `not_reported`; rule 5 told them to code an absence as a value (`none`, `open`) citing the place where the feature would be registered if it existed. A coder who searches for a rollback mechanism and finds nothing satisfies both rules, and the two independent readings of the double-coded sample split on exactly that: their notes agreed on the evidence ("no replay facility found") while one recorded a value and the other recorded silence. That single ambiguity put 19 of 38 dimensions below the 0.6 reliability threshold - `rollback` on 0.97 of its disagreements, `replayability` 0.96, `network_policy` 0.94. Rule 5 is rewritten as an ordered test: if the evidence contains the place where the feature would be declared (config schema, CLI flags, tool or plugin registry, the run loop, a documented feature list) and the feature is not there, code the absence value and cite that place at confidence at most medium; if the evidence contains no such place, code `not_reported` and name the missing place. The absence of a mention in prose is never evidence of absence, and `not_reported` is never correct once the declaring place has been opened. The change was validated before the dataset was rebuilt rather than assumed: the same 217 systems were coded twice under the revised rule, which moved pooled agreement from 0.597 to 0.879 and pooled kappa from 0.564 to 0.842, and the whole coded set was then re-coded under prompt `code-v2-2026-09-23`. The superseded coding is kept at data/coded/v1_rule5_ambiguous/ as the evidence for the change. THE CORRECTION RAISES THE HEADLINE RATE: the share of cells recorded `not_reported` rises from 26.9% to 48.9%, because prose that never mentions a feature was previously being read as evidence that the feature is absent. RQ4 is therefore larger and better founded than registered. (10) CELL STATES. A third state, `unresolved`, is added beside `not_reported` for cells the coder could not settle, so that an admission is never counted as a finding; 0.4% of released cells are unresolved. (11) CODING COMPLETE AND SCHEMA FROZEN. All 1,116 systems in the stratified coded set are coded (42,408 cells: 50.7% coded with evidence, 48.9% not_reported, 0.4% unresolved), schema v1.0 is frozen with all 38 dimensions intact - none added, removed, renamed or re-valued - and 37 of 38 dimensions clear the registered kappa >= 0.6 freeze condition. `loop_primitives` is 0.586 on exact-set match and is kept and flagged rather than redefined, because it is multi-valued and exact-set matching scores two readings as a total mismatch whenever one lists an extra primitive, while per value the readings agree on 93% of present/absent decisions (per-value kappa 0.738, Gwet's AC1 0.624). Two systems (`cai`, `pentagi`) are coded by a different model because the primary model's safety classifier stops mid-response on offensive-security agents; this is recorded per row and affects 0.2% of the set.
376-12: Searching, screening, system grouping and coding are complete; outcomes extraction is in progress. The search was frozen on 2026-09-16 (50,724 raw records, 27,747 candidates after deduplication). Title/abstract screening closed 2026-09-18 and full-text screening closed 2026-09-20: 9,967 records sought at full text, 8,435 assessed, 7,085 included, grouped into 6,162 systems. Coding of the stratified coded set closed 2026-09-23: all 1,116 systems coded on all 38 dimensions (42,408 cells), schema frozen as v1.0, and the dataset re-coded under the revised absence rule of amendment 9. All counts are in data/prisma_counts.json and the reliability figures in docs/coding_reliability.md.
376-94: Stage 1: pilot, systems coded twice independently by two model readings; the pilot was run on 217 systems rather than the registered 30, because the 20% reliability sample was available and a larger pilot costs only compute. Stage 2: per-dimension kappa between the two readings; dimensions below 0.6 are redefined or dropped; schema frozen as v1 with a changelog. Stage 3: coding of the stratified coded set (amendment 6), in two passes: pass A reads the whole evidence bundle and returns all 38 dimensions with a verbatim quote and a locator per cell; pass B re-reads only the cells pass A left unresolved, invalid or without a verbatim quote, using targeted windows of the same bundle. A deterministic 20% sample is coded a second time, independently, and BOTH codings go through the repair pass, because comparing a repaired coding against an unrepaired one measures the missing pass rather than reliability. Stage 4: outcomes extraction from papers and leaderboards. A system enters the released dataset on protocol 4.7's rule - at least 19 of 38 dimensions settled - and each cell is in one of three states: a value with evidence, `not_reported` (the sources were read and are silent, a finding), or `unresolved` (the coder could not settle it and claims nothing). Demanding all 38 would admit 77 systems of 1,116 and discard the roughly 31 cells a typical system does settle.
376-96: The coding manual (docs/coding_manual.md, frozen as v1.0) gives decision rules per dimension and two worked examples (SWE-agent, OpenHands). Rules: code the pinned version; repository beats paper when they disagree; every claimed value carries verbatim evidence; multi-valued dimensions take every applicable value. Amendment 9 rewrote the rule that separates an absence from silence, because the registered manual contradicted itself on it: an absence value is coded only when the evidence contains the place where the feature would be declared if it existed and the feature is not there, citing that place; otherwise the cell is `not_reported` and the note names the place that was missing. The absence of a mention in prose is never evidence of absence.
376-102: Cohen's kappa per dimension on the double-coded sample (217 systems, 20% of the coded set), computed between two independent readings that have both been through the repair pass, and reported in the manuscript and with the dataset. Because both readings are model readings (amendment 4), these figures measure the reproducibility of the coding procedure, not agreement with a human coder, and are reported with that meaning stated. Result: pooled agreement 0.879, pooled kappa 0.842, and 37 of 38 dimensions at or above 0.6. Two further statistics are reported beside kappa, neither replacing it: Gwet's AC1, because Cohen's kappa collapses when one category dominates and would otherwise condemn dimensions the readings agree on almost everywhere; and, for multi-valued dimensions, the mean per-value kappa, because exact-set matching scores two readings as a total mismatch whenever one lists an extra value. Per-value kappa is not substituted where it flatters - it is lower than the exact-set figure for `retry_policy` (0.491 against 0.671) and `edit_primitive` (0.589 against 0.648) - and every figure is published per dimension in data/coded/reliability_final.json.
376-106: Evidence-per-cell coding makes every value auditable and is what distinguishes this dataset from prior completeness matrices. Amendment 4 changes who does the verifying: no human verifies every cell, because 1,116 systems at 38 dimensions is 42,408 cells. Instead every claimed value carries a quote that is checked mechanically, character for character, against the exact text the coder was given, and cells that fail that check, or that fall outside their dimension's permitted values, are re-read in a repair pass and counted in the release. Nothing is coerced into a permitted value: a cell the repair pass cannot settle is published as `unresolved` rather than rounded to the nearest plausible answer, because a repaired cell would be indistinguishable from a coded one afterwards. The rates of unresolved and non-verbatim cells are reported as data-quality figures.
376-108: HARNESS-DB is released as CSV and JSON with a JSON Schema, validator and continuous integration on GitHub, with a Zenodo DOI and a Hugging Face mirror, under CC BY 4.0. Each coded cell carries its value, its evidence, a confidence, and the flag distinguishing `not_reported` from `unresolved`; the per-cell audit table (data/coded/cells.csv) additionally carries the quote, the locator, the verbatim-check result and every validation flag, so a reader can re-derive any published value. The superseded coding produced under the pre-amendment-9 absence rule is published alongside, clearly marked, because it is the evidence for the amendment.
376-116: not_reported is a first-class value: its rate per dimension is a result (RQ4), reported in data/coded/not_reported_by_dimension.csv both unweighted and weighted to the census, since strata P and O are sampled and less visible systems document less. Cells marked not_reported are excluded pairwise from association analyses; no imputation. Cells marked `unresolved` (the coder could not settle them, 0.4%) are excluded from the under-reporting rate as well, because counting an admission as a finding would inflate the result. Measured: 48.9% of cells are not_reported, against 26.9% under the ambiguous absence rule that amendment 9 replaced - the earlier figure was too low because prose that never mentions a feature was being read as evidence of its absence. The pattern is that systems document what they do and not how they are bounded: by layer, control loop 27% and meta 27% at one end, sandbox 66%, verification 66%, tool interface 63% and budgets 62% at the other; worst individually, weighted, network_policy 92.6%, replayability 90.5%, filesystem_access 87.6% and rollback 86.3%.
